title: Runtime compatibility charter and consumer migration concierge
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Define and operationalize a 'Compatibility Charter' for the serving runtime and ship a first-cut 'Migration Concierge' toolkit that guides customers and client teams through safe upgrades. This ticket consolidates policy (what counts as breaking), engineered gates (diffs/telemetry/automations), and a low-friction migration assistant (CLI + console checklist + compatibility report).
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility Charter doc published in Confluence and linked from runtime release notes
Migration Concierge prototype (rmc) can generate a compatibility report for a runtime upgrade between two runtime versions
Rollout gate playbook implemented in the release pipeline: static API diff + dynamic telemetry smoke tests + configured canary cohorts
Automated rollbacks triggered when canary latency/error thresholds are breached
Developer-facing migration checklist surfaced in Console per-release with suggested mitigations and client-adapter commands
decisions: Adopt contract-first definition: breaking change = behavioral or contract change that invalidates consumer assumptions (API shape, KV cache semantics, default tokenization, runtime ABI).
Use semantic version MAJOR for breaking behavioral/contract changes; MINOR for additive features; PATCH for bug fixes and non-behavioral changes.
Introduce a 12-month soft-deprecation window for non-security deprecations before MAJOR bump consideration; deprecations must include migration instructions and client adapter shims where feasible.
Compatibility score to be computed from static diffs and runtime smoke tests; score thresholds map to rollout policies (green = broad, amber = canary, red = blocked).
